classification.difficultyReason: Identify the required segment in nested right triangles, combine the supplied angles, calculate two lengths using exact ratios and subtract them; the equilateral part also requires constructing an altitude.

content.prompt: Find the exact value of $x$ in each of the following diagrams.

spec.description: Right triangle with base 6 extending left from the bottom-right right angle, vertical unknown x and 60-degree top-right angle. Drawing proportions are illustrative.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and x are visible.

spec.description: Upright triangle with all three sides labelled 4 and matching single edge-perpendicular equality ticks. External vertical double-headed x dimension spans base level to apex level. No altitude is supplied.
spec.mathematics: Equilateral side length 4; x is its perpendicular height.
spec.answerVisibility: The altitude construction and its half-base lengths remain solution-only.

answer.short:
$x=2\sqrt3$

Bisect the equilateral triangle into two right-angled triangles.
answer.worked:
Draw the perpendicular from the apex to the base. In an equilateral triangle it bisects the base, giving two lengths of $2$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+2^2&=4^2\\x^2&=12\\x&=2\sqrt3\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Nested right triangles share horizontal base 9 and bottom-left right angle. The inner slope forms 30 degrees with the base; the outer slope is another 15 degrees above it. An outside leader identifies the 15-degree sector. x labels only the upper segment of the left vertical side.
spec.mathematics: Total angle at the rightmost vertex is 45 degrees; x is the difference between the two vertical heights.
spec.answerVisibility: No total angle, calculated height or answer is added to the student figure.

answer.short:
$x=9-3\sqrt3$

Subtract the smaller triangle’s height from the larger triangle’s height.
answer.worked:
The larger triangle has angle $30^\circ+15^\circ=45^\circ$ at the rightmost vertex. Let the larger and smaller vertical heights be $H$ and $h$.
$$\begin{align*}H&=9\tan45^\circ\\H&=9\\h&=9\tan30^\circ\\h&=3\sqrt3\\x&=H-h\\x&=9-3\sqrt3\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Nested right triangles share the vertical side labelled 20. The inner and outer base intersections have interior angles 45 degrees and 30 degrees respectively. The external horizontal double-headed x dimension spans only the base segment between those intersections.
spec.mathematics: x equals the larger adjacent length minus the smaller adjacent length.
spec.answerVisibility: Calculated base lengths and the final difference are solution-only.

answer.short:
$x=20\sqrt3-20$

Subtract the smaller base length from the larger base length.
answer.worked:
Let the larger and smaller base lengths, measured from the left right angle, be $B$ and $b$.
$$\begin{align*}B&=\frac{20}{\tan30^\circ}\\B&=20\sqrt3\\b&=\frac{20}{\tan45^\circ}\\b&=20\\x&=B-b\\x&=20\sqrt3-20\end{align*}$$
